content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I am still learning how to use [company_name] [product_name] and am creating my first control program for a conveyor. I've managed to operate the conveyor via the PLC. My next task is to add functions for start, stop, and reset. The reset button is intended for situations where the emergency stop is pressed and then released, so all positions can be homed. I need guidance on integrating these three features into my program. I've attached my current progress for reference.

Hello [user_name], welcome to the forum. Your program appears quite confusing, which makes it hard to grasp your intended process. It's best if you organize your work and give a detailed description of your entire project. Could you clarify what you mean when you say 'if the distress call is pressed and then released, all positions are reset'? If you're using an emergency stop and reset, [product_name] is not certified for this function in my region. Automatically resetting to a basic position could also present safety risks. If you mean a general reset (not linked to emergency stop), can you specify what the basic position is supposed to be? Regards, [user_name]

The conveyor system is comprised of two identical sections. One lifts the tray from the conveyor, and the other lowers the tray back onto it. When a tray arrives, a part presence sensor locks the position valve, preventing movement, and signals the motor to move downward. Upon reaching the bottom limit switch, a piston activates and a second motor moves the tray inward. Each tray has metal parts that are counted as they pass the sensor; after the second count, the piston closes. Another part presence sensor stops the motor from moving further, and the up/down motor lifts the tray. If the tray reaches the upper limit, the supply is cut, and the straight motor moves the tray back onto the conveyor. At the top, another sensor counts to two again to open the piston for the next tray, and the same sequence happens inversely on the other side. I hope this explanation clarifies my program's functionality. I now need help setting up start to begin the sequence, stop as an emergency action, emergency buttons, and a reset button to ensure all components are safe before restarting the cycle after interruptions.
It's unclear to me how you'd know the required sequence of your process but struggle to implement a start/stop function. Typically, programming begins with the start function.
I understand, and that's the challenge I'm facing—how to properly define the start function. Do I need to use a switch incorporating all relevant inputs?
So what exactly is the starting position? And why not build your program as a clear series of steps? There should always be a defined start and end position.

The starting position is at the top, where the conveyor runs continuously and moves the tray into the lifting sequence. Then, the bottom conveyor operates with a similar lifting process. I'd really appreciate advice on structuring the sequence better. As mentioned earlier, I'm fairly new to this field.

analysis.insight_summary: The main difficulty for the user is implementing start, stop, and reset functions in a conveyor control program using [company_name] PLC hardware. Users need clearer methods for organizing sequences and managing emergency and reset actions safely. A lack of detailed instructions and logical programming structure creates confusion, especially for newcomers in situations involving system safety. Managing control of multiple components further stresses the importance of program templates or structured approaches for safe and reliable operation.
analysis.user_expectations: The user seeks detailed suggestions on programming start, stop, and reset features, specifically on safely managing system statuses after emergencies. There is also an expectation for guidance on creating a well-structured sequence that ensures operational safety and reliability.
